In its operation of the Base Rate, the Bank, while supporting the economy’s continuing recovery of growth, will place its emphasis on keeping consumer price inflation within the inflation target range over a medium term horizon.

However, the Bank will carefully examine the possibility of fall in inflation expectations causing second-round effects and thereby weakening economic dynamism, as well as the possibility of the current trend of inflation persisting due to the slowdown in global economic growth and to global low inflation.

The Bank will prepare for the possibility of any expansion in financial and foreign exchange market volatility resulting for instance from sudden capital in- and outflows, and respond effectively should emergencies occur, while paying attention to changes in values of major currencies.
5. Strengthening Support for SMEs and Maximizing Its

The Bank will strengthen its financial support for SMEs, and maximize the effectiveness of that support, by actively utilizing its Bank Intermediated Lending Support Facility (formerly Aggregate Credit Ceiling Loans), its main credit policy instrument.

The Bank will work to alleviate the volatility of foreign investors’ securities investment fund flows, by enhancing the shock absorption capacity of the exchange rate and carrying out its macroeconomic management in a stable and consistent manner, while implementing appropriate measures to stabilize the financial and FX markets related to any herd behavior in market expectations.
As necessary, it will in consultation with the government devise market stabilization measures, for example by flexibly implementing its macroprudential policies for the foreign exchange sector.

It will work to improve the method of program operation so as to increase the incentives for financial institutions to expand their SME lending and to meet, within the scope of original policy aim, the funding demand of SMEs.

In order to complement its monetary policy and ease financial pro-cyclicality, the Bank will flexibly adjust the ceiling on its Bank Intermediated Lending Support Facility and the related sub-programs, by closely checking the financial and economic situation and SME funding conditions.

The Bank will also strengthen its monitoring of risk factors including the possibility of financial instability in EMEs, affected by the US QE tapering, spreading to the Korean economy, while continuing to review and improve
its comprehensive stage-by-stage Contingency Plan.
